newsitem.title: USA: U.S., France begin 'open skies' aviation talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S., France begin 'open skies' aviation talks.

text.p: The United States and France on Tuesday opened three days of talks toward a free-market "open skies" aviation agreement that would end restrictions on airline flights between the two countries.

U.S. officials said Washington would continue its effort to win approval of the "open skies" plan, but did not expect any immediate agreement by Paris. A previous set of talks was held in Paris last December.

France broke its aviation agreement with the United States in 1993 on grounds the United States wanted too many new routes, but bilateral traffic has continued with each side approving new fares on a seasonal, ad hoc basis.
The free market accord that the United States wants with France is similar to agreements in force with many other countries, including Germany, the Netherlands and Canada.
These give airlines in each country the right to serve as many airports in the other country as often as they wish and to carry passengers beyond into a third country.
